Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

use verb

also employ, make use of, use up, use your dictionary, make the best use of, use a word in a sentence

ūtor, ūtī, ūsus sum

verb, third conjugation, deponent; with the ablative

use, make use of

The thing used is in the ablative: oculīs ūtī, cōnsiliō ūtī. Ūtī also means “enjoy, have the benefit of” and “treat (someone)”.

Other words

  • adhibeō, adhibēre, adhibuī, adhibitum — apply, bring to bear

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 36: tantum cibī et pōtiōnis adhibendum

    To bring something in for a purpose: care, force, a doctor.

Examples

  • Certē oculīs ūtere.

    (— Is that Epidicus I see? —) You certainly have the use of your eyes.Plaut. Epid. 1.1.4 (Lewis & Short)

  • dē rēbus ipsīs ūtere tuō jūdiciō

    on the matter itself, use your own judgementCic. Off. 1.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • Ūtere (ūtiminī) dictiōnāriō.

    Use your dictionary.Traupman 34

  • optimē ūtī (+ ablative)

    to make the best use ofTraupman 401

  • Pōne «legō» in sententiā.

    Use “legō” in a sentence.Traupman 401

See also useful, employ.
